title.narrative: Strengthening Adaptive and Inclusive Food Systems for Improved Nutrition and Climate Resilience in South Asia

description.narrative: The overall objective in Bangladesh is to improve food security and nutrition of vulnerable communities through inclusive, climate-resilient and locally anchored food systems. The project aims to strengthen cross-sectoral governance, empower local leaders and women, and institutionalise nutrition-sensitive planning at local government level. As a result, communities improve dietary diversity, resilience to climate shocks and income opportunities, while local authorities better integrate nutrition into development planning and service delivery.

The project directly engages approximately 200 Food and Nutrition Systems Champions, local government officials, leaders of women’s groups and farmers’ associations, and staff of partner organisations (FIVDB and WAVE) in Netrokona district through structured capacity-building and coordination activities. Indirectly, the project reaches around 21,500 people (approximately 7,500 men and 14,000 women) in vulnerable rural households who benefit from improved food systems, nutrition-sensitive services and strengthened local governance. Women smallholder farmers and women leaders are prioritised as key change agents, particularly in nutrition, livelihoods and community-level decision-making.

This phase expands and strengthens the NSC model by introducing sub-regional structures – Community Collectives – that expand local value webs through Learning Hubs, fostering innovation, knowledge exchange, and economic resilience. Unlike linear value chains, value webs are dynamic, decentralized, and interconnected systems, continuously growing beyond individual communities. They enable circular flows of knowledge, economic exchange, and resources, strengthening food system resilience and self-reliance. Therefore, the Nutrition Smart Community (NSC) approach will complement the project (NSC III) by strengthening governance linkages and enhancing the capacity of local governments, farmers, and SMEs to adopt nutrition-sensitive food systems.However, to achieve larger systems transformation, the new NSC iii must now evolve by forging stronger connections to higher governance levels and adopting a systematic scale-linking approach. This focuses i) Collaboration Networks & Leadership for Systemic Transformation (All Levels) ii) Adaptive & Inclusive Governance for Multisectoral Action (Meso Level) iii) Decentralized Learning & Local Economic Reinforcement (Micro/Sub-Regional Level).
